title: Nonparametric rolling-sentry for per-slice throughput & p95 stability
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Design and implement a nonparametric, rolling-window regression detector ("Sentry") that evaluates per-slice throughput (tokens/sec) and latency p95 in PR CI. The goal is to reduce false positives from nonstationary traffic by using bootstrapped confidence intervals, rank-based drift tests, and an adaptive sample-size policy. It should emit a deterministic gating decision (pass/warn/fail) for PRs and produce human-readable diagnostics for triage.
background: Current CI gates rely on single-point comparisons to a static baseline which frequently flags harmless variance as regressions or misses subtle long-tail shifts. We need a more robust detector that handles skewed distributions (heavy tails) and workload nonstationarity introduced by recent KV-cache changes and dynamic batching heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Detector runs in CI within the 15m PR timeout budget for standard smoke suite
False positive rate <= 2% on a 90-day historic sample of benign PRs
True positive detection of injected 7% tokens/sec degradation and 15% p95 tail increase in synthetic experiments
Gating decision output includes: baseline slice id, sample sizes, bootstrap CI, p-value (rank test), and suggested rollback risk level
Artifacts: GH Action step + canonical dashboard panel + confluence runbook for oncall triage
design_notes: Use rolling-window baselines (N windows of 24h) to allow short-term shifts without manual baseline flips
Primary statistics: tokens/sec median and 95th percentile latency using bootstrap CIs with 1000 resamples
Statistical test: Mann-Whitney U / Wilcoxon rank-sum for throughput + two-sided rank test for p95 slices; supplement with Kolmogorov-Smirnov when distributions diverge
Adaptive sampling: increase sample size for low-signal slices up to a configured cap to avoid noisy decisions
Slice selection: prioritize slices by entropy and recent error-rate correlation (we already capture this in the smoke harness)
Decision policy: three-state output (pass/warn/fail). Warn becomes failure for protected branches (release/*).
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype detector as a standalone Python job that consumes archived CI traces and produces a report (2w)
Phase 2: Integrate into GH Actions as an optional step for feature branches with feature flag gating (1w)
Phase 3: Add dashboard tiles and auto-linking from GH comment with diagnostic artifacts (1w)
Phase 4: Run shadow mode on all PRs for 2 weeks and tune thresholds, then flip to hard gating for release branches (2w)
test_plan: Historic replay: run detector across 90 days of PR traces and measure FP/FN rates
Injection suite: synthetic perturbations for tokens/sec (-5%, -7%, -12%) and p95 (+10%, +15%, +30%) to evaluate sensitivity
Stress tests: ensure detector scales to 200 concurrent PR checks within CI minutes budget
A/B run with current gate for 2 weeks to compare triage burden and incident amplification
results_summary: Prototype bootstrap detector flagged injected regressions reliably in synthetic runs (7% drop tokens/sec and 15% p95 increase detected with p<0.01). Historic replay shows FP ~3.5% with conservative thresholds; target tuning reduced it to ~1.8% during shadow run. Median runtime per check ~4.6m on CI runners.
open_risks: CI compute cost may increase as adaptive sampling upsizes for low-volume slices
Complexity in communicating three-state decisions to non-engineering reviewers
Edge cases where transient infra noise (network blips) produces correlated p95 spikes across baselines
mitigations: Rate-limit adaptive upsampling per PR and fall back to lighter statistical summary if budget exceeded
Add a concise human-friendly verdict section in GH comments with suggested next steps and links to detailed plots
Correlation detector to suppress gating if cross-region network event is detected within a short window
